background: This is the Neo-Assyrian setting, with Urartu to the north, Babylonia to the south and multiple principalities and coastal communities in the west. Neo-Hittite states belong to this landscape; they are not the earlier Bronze Age Hittite empire. Israel and Judah are separate campaign powers.
abstractions: Later Assyrian conquests are not starting borders. Neo-Hittite, Aramean, Phoenician, Greek and Median groupings compress politically diverse communities; the Median seat is not a later united empire. Archaeological centers, approximate chronology and designed starting forces are explained in the maintained Near East brief.
validation: Provisional recommendations: playable IDs, opening city networks, one army per regular seat and Phoenicia's starting fleet checked. Human difficulty, balance and mountain-crossing routes have not been playtested for this guidance.

powers.advice: Suggested for a land-focused campaign around the Assyrian city network. One starting army cannot cover every direction; inspect northern and southern routes before choosing the first front.
Suggested for coastal holdings and a starting fleet. Transport opens several approaches, while the narrow coastal position makes landing locations and local supply important.
A southern alternative with several cities but no starting fleet in this period. Plan around your land connections; do not assume the Bronze Age Egyptian naval opening applies here.
A smaller northern city network with terrain-sensitive approaches. Inspect which routes are actually passable under the current movement rules before planning a southern advance.
A compact city base among neighboring regional powers. Consider a limited first objective and available supply; the small territory makes this a different opening rather than a verified easy start.
